findings.text: the fragment attributes the refused promotion to "the landing commit's retry bound (twelve attempts half a second apart, about six seconds)", but at the revision the fragment names, 1d16388a31, reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2080-2081 sets _INDEX_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 130 at 0.5 s intervals (about 65 s), and the refused promotion's whole run took 4.87 s, so no retry bound of either length was exhausted; the six-second figure is the staging wait misapplied to the landing commit, and a reader acting on it would lengthen a bound that never ran.
the manifest records `commits: PENDING_SHA`, so it names no commit for the coordinator to resolve; the landed head had to be recovered from classification.json rather than from the record itself.

every test_logs path and measurement_module points under /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261114T143927859241-.../, which no longer exists at review time, so the raw measurement evidence is unreadable and the numbers survive only inside the run's stream.jsonl.

the checkpoint and rubric.completeness claim "3 pre-revision attempts (10 promotions)", while the run's stream records nine landed promotions across pre-arm-3, pre-arm-4 and pre-arm-5 and six further runs in pre-arm-1 and pre-arm-2 that exited 2 without reaching code, so the manifest's "10" and the fragment's "nine in all" cannot both be right.
